title: "Eorin Baekseong" Did Not Mean Children
hook: In the preface to Hunminjeongeum, the word "eorida" meant foolish, not young
summary: In the 15th century "eorida" meant foolish. The sense of "young" appeared from the 16th century and is the main meaning today.

text: The Hunminjeongeum book made under King Sejong.
A version of it written out in Hangul has the line "eorin baekseong i nireugojyeo bae isyeodo."

panels.mean: In the 15th century it meant foolish

panels.text: So a "child" was originally a foolish person?

text: From the 16th century the sense of "young" appeared.
Over time it became the main meaning.
It shows up in texts from the 17th century.

panels.text: Word meanings just drift wherever they like

sources: National Institute of Korean Language: Eorida and Eoriseokda
National Institute of Korean Language: Origin of Eorini
